newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Troops arrive for NATO-backed Baltic exercise.
newsitem.headline: Troops arrive for NATO-backed Baltic exercise.

text.p: The first of more than 2,500 troops arrived in Estonia on Thursday for a NATO-backed exercise called Baltic Challenge '97, officials said.

The arrival of detachments of 1,400 U.S. troops along with units from Estonia, fellow Baltic states Latvia and Lithuania as well as Nordic soldiers follows two days after the Balts were officially refused early NATO entry at the Madrid summit.
The Estonian defence ministry said the July 13-22 exercise was the second largest this year in Europe.
The exercise is part of NATO's Partnership for Peace (PfP) programme, which offers cooperation but no security guarantees.
PfP is the main way the Balts, independent from the former Soviet Union since 1991, are building links with the alliance.
U.S. Marine Corps Master Gunnery Sergeant Tom Adams, one of the spokesmen for the exercise, said around 2,000 of the 2,600 troops taking part would be in Estonia by the end of the day.
Two U.S. supply ships have also anchored near Tallinn port and two military aircraft were due to arrive during the day.

"Baltic Challenge '97 is a high level peacekeeping exercise, in which the goal is to involve the cooperation of the Baltic Sea countries and the U.S. military in peacekeeping operations," the defence ministry said in a statement.
The exercise is to take place near the northwestern town of Paldiski, a former Soviet nuclear submarine training base.
